clue.text: Gallnut forming wad round inside tree

indicators.note: turning something round sends it the other way, so the word for wad is read backwards
one piece is placed inside another, here the turned wad within the tree

blocks.note: a pad is a wad of soft material
a common deciduous tree

explanation.surface: A gall on a tree takes shape as a lump of tissue wrapped round inside the wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned pad goes into the maple after its first two letters: MA-DAP-PLE gives MADAPPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists mad-apple as a name for an oak gall, the round growth also called a gallnut.

clue.text: M missing on 'mongrel'

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the following little word is dropped from the longer one

blocks.note: printers call the em space a mutton, to keep it apart from the en, a nut
taken as written: the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the letter M has been left off a label reading mongrel.
explanation.walkthrough: M has to be read as the printer's em, whose trade name is mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutt is informal for a dog of mixed or unknown breed, the same as a mongrel.

clue.text: Navajo, possibly, heroin held in palm as container

indicators.note: something held in another is enclosed by it, so the drug goes within the tree

blocks.note: H is slang for heroin
atap is the nipa palm of South-East Asia
taken as written
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A Navajo hides heroin in the hollow of a palm tree, using it as a stash.
explanation.walkthrough: Atap, or attap, is the Malay name for the nipa palm whose leaves thatch houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Navajo belongs to the Athapascan language family of North America, so it is one example; 'possibly' marks that.

clue.text: Dip in river? On the contrary, soak

indicators.note: one thing in another sits within it
this flips the stated order, so the second item holds the first instead of sitting inside it

blocks.note: to dunk is to dip, as a biscuit in tea
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick plunge into a river, or rather gets drenched.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the dip goes inside the river; 'On the contrary' reverses that, putting R inside DUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: A soak is a heavy drinker, and so is a drunk, both nouns for a habitual drinker.

clue.text: Priest copying Latin?

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for priest
apish behaviour imitates others, as an ape copies

explanation.surface: A cleric imitates Latin in his services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' here means belonging to the Latin, or Roman Catholic, Church; the question mark flags this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Papish is an old, hostile adjective for Roman Catholic, and the Roman Church is the Latin rite.

clue.text: Supplement getting us into lido

indicators.note: putting something into another places it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
plage is a beach or seaside bathing resort, a lido

explanation.surface: An extra fee gets the group admitted to the open-air pool.
explanation.walkthrough: US goes after the first two letters of the beach word: PL-US-AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plusage is a rare word for an extra amount or surplus, so something added on as a supplement.

clue.text: Raises iris, round pink 'un

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the flower wraps the newspaper

blocks.note: lis is the heraldic lily or iris, as in fleur-de-lis
the Financial Times, printed on pink paper and nicknamed the pink 'un

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts a pink iris to look round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to raise it up, so the two verbs in the third person match.

clue.text: Email 'post'? I.e. _, lot junked

indicators.note: junked letters are scrapped and thrown together, so the remaining set is jumbled before it is used

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, the two letters to be taken away
taken as written, three more letters to be taken away

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a mailed message counts as a 'post', followed by a cryptic gap to be filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the blank stands for the answer, and the answer plus I.E. and LOT is a jumble of EMAIL POST. Rearrange those nine letters as SPAM-IE-LOT and drop IE and LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited junk electronic mail, a mass 'posting' sent to many inboxes at once.

clue.text: Swede maybe from Cretan town, in tin

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: Candia is the old Venetian name for Heraklion, Crete's chief town
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A Swedish tourist comes from a Cretan town carrying a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swede' looks like the vegetable, a turnip-like root; here it is a person from Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandian means a Scandinavian, and a Swede is one example of a Scandinavian, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Grind for poet, page badly written down

indicators.note: badly written letters come out in the wrong order and need rearranging

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer at the grind of poetry scrawls a page badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for poet' marks a poetic spelling, here Spenser's.
explanation.definitionFit: Powne or pownd is Spenser's spelling of pound, which means to crush or grind into small pieces.

clue.text: Tipsier than the rest, go astray in wayward times

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
something wayward refuses to keep its course, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: to err is to stray from what is right
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: At a drunken party, the tipsiest guest wanders off at odd moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry is a gentle word for slightly drunk, so the superlative describes whoever is most tipsy of all.

clue.text: What one's actually got to spend in Trincomalee, lacking capital, bust (10, two words)

definitions.text: What one's actually got to spend

indicators.note: capital here is the opening letter, and lacking it means that first letter is dropped
something bust is broken, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: a port city in Sri Lanka, taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller in a Sri Lankan port, broke, works out what money is really left to spend.
explanation.walkthrough: Trincomalee without its T leaves ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists use the term for earnings adjusted for inflation, the true buying power someone has to spend.

clue.text: Beat time and drone quietly

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a drone is a low continuous hum
p for piano, the musical direction to play softly

explanation.surface: A drummer keeps time while a low drone plays softly underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump is to strike with heavy blows, a close synonym of beat as a verb.

clue.text: Rare fiddle player maybe met the queen

blocks.note: if you saw a friend yesterday, you met them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: An unusual violinist was once introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' belongs to the definition: it flags a word seldom used, as Azed often does.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawer is one who saws, and a violinist is jokingly said to saw at the strings with the bow.

clue.text: Unearthing former hominid clutching odd pieces of tripod

indicators.note: odd pieces are those in the odd-numbered positions, first, third and fifth
clutching something holds it inside, so the creature encloses the chosen letters

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
humans are hominids
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digging up an early ape-man finds it gripping parts of a three-legged stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former hominid' reads as one extinct creature, but 'former' and 'hominid' clue separately: an ex-human.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumation is the digging up of something buried, especially a body, so unearthing in the noun sense.

clue.text: Military station, site adapted for deputy PM

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

blocks.note: tana or thana, an Indian word for a military or police post
taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: An army base and its grounds are converted for use by a deputy prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: TANA is an Anglo-Indian term found in Chambers. The answer is the Irish title Tanaiste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tanaiste is the deputy head of the Irish government, second to the Taoiseach, its prime minister.

clue.text: Dunderhead in charge in support unit? Turnip perhaps

indicators.note: the second in places what comes before it inside the garment named next

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
a bra is a supporting undergarment, a single item of support

explanation.surface: A blockhead put in command of a support unit is called a turnip.
explanation.walkthrough: Turnip is also slang for a dimwit, tempting the solver to read the clue as a definition of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the cabbage genus, and the turnip is one member, hence 'perhaps' for an example.

clue.text: A leader put in prison, divinely symbolic

indicators.note: putting someone in prison encloses them, so the first pieces go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
Il Duce, the title of Mussolini, Italian for leader
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A dictator thrown into jail is made a sacred symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Caducean means of the caduceus, the herald's wand of the god Hermes, so an emblem tied to a deity.

clue.text: Supreme attainment one divine found in his wandering

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it, so the first pieces go within the second
wandering letters stray from their places and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a divine being a clergyman
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman reaches the summit of spiritual achievement during his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun here, a clergyman, which is why it yields the degree abbreviation for a Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist teaching siddhi is perfection or the highest spiritual accomplishment, including supernatural powers.

clue.text: Oriental chief uniting Egyptian and Hebrew gods

indicators.note: uniting two things joins them side by side, so the two names are set end to end

blocks.note: Ra, the Egyptian sun god
Jah, a short form of Jehovah, the Hebrew name of God

explanation.surface: An Eastern ruler brings together the deities of two ancient peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gods' does duty for both names: an Egyptian god and a Hebrew one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah is an Indian king or prince, a ruler from the East in older usage.

clue.text: Scrub army regulation briefly during dance

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the initials of army regulation
a gigue is a lively baroque dance, the French jig

explanation.surface: A military order cuts a dance short and cancels it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrub' looks like a verb meaning cancel; it is the noun for low bushy vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Garigue is the low, open scrubland of aromatic shrubs found on dry Mediterranean limestone hills.

clue.text: Living organisms causing sickness in tropical birds

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: mal is French for illness, as in grand mal
the ani is a black cuckoo of tropical America

explanation.surface: Microbes spread disease among parrots and other tropical birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The illness goes after the third letter: ANI-MAL-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are living creatures, multicellular organisms that feed and move, matching the plural noun.

clue.text: Slap once used and abused

indicators.note: abused words are mistreated and knocked out of their proper order

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls being struck long ago, then exploited and mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slap' is the adverb, as in 'slap in the middle', meaning abruptly; 'once' marks the answer as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Asudden is an old word for suddenly, and slap as an adverb means suddenly or without warning.

clue.text: Greases Scottish palms, changing two odd characters, getting place on board

indicators.note: odd characters are those in the first, third and fifth positions of a word, the places involved in the swap
changing two letters means a pair is swapped out for others while the rest of the word stays put

blocks.note: taken as written; its first and third letters are the ones replaced
to ship is to place on board, and the odd letters of the plural form supply the replacements

explanation.surface: Someone bribing officials north of the border, swapping a couple of strange characters to win a seat on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: PALMS and SHIPS (places on board) both have S as their fifth letter; replacing the other two odd letters of palms, P and L, with those of ships, S and I, gives SAIMS. 'Greases palms' looks like bribery, but 'palms' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Saim is the Scots word for lard or fat, and as a verb it means to smear with grease.

clue.text: Female with child no showing by time in fifth month

indicators.note: with no showing of the following letters, they vanish from the word for a child

blocks.note: she, a female
a baby is a young child
taken as written: the letters to remove
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman expecting a baby is not yet showing by the fifth month of pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pregnancy picture is a decoy: the month is in the Jewish calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebat is the fifth month of the Jewish civil year, falling around January and February.

clue.text: It's cushty manoeuvring canal boat

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things about into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: British slang for great or comfortable, taken as written

explanation.surface: Steering a narrowboat along the canal is pleasantly easy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cushty is London slang, popularised by the sitcom Only Fools and Horses, for excellent or easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A schuyt is a Dutch flat-bottomed vessel used on inland waterways, so a canal boat.

clue.text: Hardy novel portraying manifold evil

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is given a new arrangement

blocks.note: the novelist's surname, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel depicts evil in many forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun after Hardy's name; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed Hydra grew two heads for each one cut off, so the name is used for any many-sided evil.

clue.text: Maori funeral, pungent on the ear

indicators.note: what lands on the ear is heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: tangy, sharp and pungent in taste or smell

explanation.surface: At a Maori funeral, a sharp smell hangs in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangi is a Maori ceremony of mourning held before a burial, often over several days.

clue.text: Get excited about new salon solution

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word goes round the letter

blocks.note: to rise is to become stirred up or roused
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A client gets thrilled about a new hair treatment at the salon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rinse is a liquid tint or conditioner a hairdresser washes through the hair.

clue.text: Blow, hard, catches a gull heading for nest in Scotland

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so the first pair of pieces closes round the rest

blocks.note: a hit is a blow
H, the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
taken as written
the mew or sea-mew is a gull

explanation.surface: A gale buffets a seagull returning to its nest on a Scottish shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea-mew is an old name for a gull. The whole of 'heading for nest in Scotland' is the definition: the answer is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamewith is a Scots adverb meaning homewards, and a bird making for its nest is on its way home.

clue.text: Split decapitated fish

indicators.note: a decapitated word has lost its head, its first letter

blocks.note: a shake is a split or crack in timber

explanation.walkthrough: 'Split decapitated fish' reads as a fish cut open; a shake is a carpenter's word for a crack in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The hake is a large food fish of the cod family, so the answer is one kind of fish.

clue.text: Last part of book possibly penned by Colin Dexter

indicators.note: something penned by a name is written inside it, so the letters sit within those words

blocks.note: found across the gap between the author's first name and surname

explanation.surface: The closing chapter of a Morse novel was written by its author, Colin Dexter.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabetical list of topics usually comes at the very back of a book, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Moldovan money accepted, almost all taken from Balkan state financier (Indian)

blocks.note: bani are the small coins of Moldova, a hundred to the leu
A is the abbreviation for accepted

blocks.clueFragment: almost all taken from Balkan state
blocks.note: a second route to the same letters: Albania with AL, most of all, removed

explanation.surface: A Moldovan coin is accepted after nearly everything is withdrawn from a Balkan banker.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed gives two routes here: BANI plus A, and Albania less its first two letters, which spell most of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bania or banyan is a Hindu trader or moneylender, the merchant caste that handled finance in India.

clue.text: Member of woodwind summoned in swinging social (10, two words)

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
swinging things move freely about, so the letters of the party word are jumbled

blocks.note: rang for someone, called them
a social is a party, taken as written

explanation.surface: An oboe-type player was called in to a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a tenor reed instrument of the oboe family, part of an orchestra's woodwind section.

clue.text: Middle of day and muezzin's given one?

definitions.text: Middle of day and muezzin's given one?

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, and here it applies to both nouns that follow
given here means with something added on, so a last piece is tacked onto the end

blocks.note: the centre letter of the three
the centre letter of the seven
an is the article meaning one, as in 'an apple'

explanation.surface: At noon the mosque's crier has issued his summons once again.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: around midday the muezzin has given one, a call to prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The azan is the Muslim call to prayer, chanted by the muezzin five times a day, including at noon.

clue.text: What is after c for cyanite?!

blocks.note: answer the riddle in full: what comes after c? d, and then e

explanation.surface: A riddle about the alphabet is offered as the gloss for a blue mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a riddle, the reply is 'D is then E', which run together gives DISTHENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Disthene is an alternative mineral name for kyanite, also spelt cyanite, a blue aluminium silicate.
